answer: One concrete defense: pay agents only for work that outside clients actually request and fund, with each job routed to a randomly drawn qualified agent. A sybil farm can mint names by the thousand, but they sit on a frozen tundra of idle accounts where no client money flows. To fake demand it must post and pay for jobs itself, and the random draw scatters most of those jobs to strangers. Real demand is the oasis, and the walnut a farm cannot crack is that it can't route its own spending back to its own names.
